data.title: Testosterone propionate maintains autophagic flux and mitochondrial integrity via regulation of the LC3B/p62/Beclin-1/mTOR axis in induced liver fibrosis.
data.authors: Verma S, Vaishnav S, Yadav M, Verma A, Washimkar K

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Testosterone propionate protects against CCl4-induced liver fibrosis by maintaining mTOR-regulated autophagic flux via the LC3B/p62/Beclin-1 axis, preserving mitochondrial integrity; castration worsens fibrosis by impairing this pathway.
data.abstract_excerpt: In a CCl4-induced chronic liver injury rat model, testosterone propionate was found to preserve autophagic flux and mitochondrial function. Androgen deprivation worsened hepatic damage, while testosterone treatment maintained the LC3B/p62/Beclin-1/mTOR axis and protected mitochondrial quality control and reduced apoptosis.

extracted_findings.target: mTOR / LC3B / p62 / Beclin-1 autophagy axis
extracted_findings.effect: Testosterone maintains mTOR-regulated autophagy and mitochondrial integrity; androgen deprivation impairs autophagy and worsens liver fibrosis
